trust_decision.summary: The URI host must be a single authority host (no control chars, no / ? # @ or backslash, no bare colon, brackets balanced) so getHost()/getAuthority() cannot disagree with the on-wire Host header; decided in Uri::assertValidHost, which is fed by the bracket-preserving pre-encoding regex in Uri::parse.

landing_point.why: A reader of "weak URI host validation" goes to the only host check in the class: the control-character regex in assertValidHost; the first hunk of the real fix is elsewhere, in Uri::parse.

fix_sites.entry_point: new Uri($url) / Uri::__construct(); Message::parseRequest() absolute-form target
fix_sites.module_kind: uri_parser (private static, URL string -> components before parse_url/urlencode)

fix_sites.entry_point: Request::__construct()/Request::withUri() via Uri::assertValidHost; ServerRequest::getUriFromGlobals() via withHost()

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Utils::modifyRequest only echoes the caller's own UriInterface::getHost() into a Host header; the URI implementation owns its host, so a request-modification helper is not a validation point - and the header it builds is later set through withHeader(), which already rejects CRLF.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Host:port assembly must keep working: Request validates the bare host and only then appends getPort() (example.com + 8080 -> "example.com:8080"), so a fix that validates the assembled value rejects every request with a port. Likewise bracket hosts with non-IPv6 contents must stay accepted ([gggg::1], [], [a]b], [fe80::1%25eth0], IDN hosts), so copying Rfc7230::isValidHostHeaderHost's filter_var/IPvFuture check into Uri::assertValidHost breaks legitimate values the fix's own tests pin as accepted.

O6_input_shapes: host string returned by a foreign Psr\Http\Message\UriInterface::getHost() when Request generates the Host header
absolute-form request target inside a message string parsed by Message::parseRequest()
bracketed vs unbracketed literals, and bracketed hosts whose contents are not valid IPv6 (zone ids, empty brackets)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Utils::modifyRequest() copies $changes['uri']->getHost() straight into a Host header (and Host:port) with no Uri::assertValidHost call, then reapplies headers through withHeader(), which only rejects CR/LF.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a convenience helper: the caller supplied the UriInterface, so the URI implementation is responsible for its own host, and the helper is not a parser or a validation boundary.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one file away from the landing point in the same package; a request-mutation helper that a report about URI parsing would not name

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Request::withUri($uri, true) keeps the existing Host header and skips updateHostFromUri(), so a foreign UriInterface whose getHost() contains a delimiter is stored on the request unvalidated while the fix's tests only cover Request::__construct().
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: preserveHost=true is an explicit opt-in: the Host header is deliberately the caller's own and the URI is a foreign PSR-7 object, so no header is generated and there is nothing to validate.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the Host-header generation the fix exercises, but a different branch a few lines away

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Message::toString() writes 'Host: '.$message->getUri()->getHost() into the serialized message with no validation and no port, for any RequestInterface that has no host header.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: For this library's own Request the branch is unreachable (a Host header always exists when the host is non-empty), so it only matters for third-party RequestInterface implementations.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: serialization layer in src/Message.php, a different concern from URI validation

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another request-mutation helper that hand-builds the Host header from getHost() without Uri::assertValidHost.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: modifyRequest already hand-builds Host at src/Utils.php:223 and src/Utils.php:265 instead of delegating to Uri/Request, so a maintainer adding a helper would copy that pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second authority-to-URI builder (parseRequestUri) that re-assembles scheme://host/path itself with its own ':443' heuristic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already re-implements authority handling rather than delegating to Uri, so a sibling that special-cases brackets or ports is a natural extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third host validator beside Uri::assertValidHost, with stricter IPv6/IPvFuture logic.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix aligns Uri's delimiter regex with the one already present here, so divergence between the two validators is the recurring maintenance pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A normalization path that rewrites the host component through withHost()/fromParts() based on scheme flags.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: UriNormalizer already branches on the host for the file scheme, so a maintainer could add host rewriting there without going through a request.

O9_family: URI host parsing differential / host confusion (CWE-20 improper input validation, CWE-436 interpretation conflict)

O10_build.toolchain: composer install; PHPUnit 8.5/9.6 on php ^7.2.5 || ^8.0; symfony polyfills; no extensions beyond standard
O10_build.project_tests: tests/UriTest.php, tests/RequestTest.php, tests/ServerRequestTest.php, tests/MessageTest.php, tests/UtilsTest.php (PHPUnit; pure string/array handling, no network)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add / ? # @ and backslash to the assertValidHost control-character regex and stop there, leaving Uri::parse's bracket-preservation regex (and the bracket/colon checks) and Utils::modifyRequest's Host-header construction untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: src/Rfc7230.php:69-93 already implements a stricter duplicate of the host check; it is not vulnerable at the pinned commit and was not pursued.
